tagline: SC 11 under its older name, through Pickens's own country.
intro: The name came first. When the state made all of SC 11 the Cherokee Foothills Scenic Highway, it provided that the stretch in Oconee and Pickens counties would continue to be known as the Andrew Pickens Scenic Parkway. Pickens was a militia general of the Revolution, later given the name Skyagunsta, the Wizard Owl.

It starts at Exit 1 of I-85, under a mile from Georgia, and runs north through Walhalla toward the Blue Ridge. In Pickens County bridges carry it over Lake Keowee, and it passes near Table Rock before it reaches Greenville County.

moments.title: Tamassee
moments.text: Ambushed near the Cherokee town here in 1776, Andrew Pickens's outnumbered militia fought in a ring within a ring, one firing while the other reloaded. He died near Tamassee in 1817.

moments.title: Keowee-Toxaway State Park
moments.text: Made in 1970 from Duke Power land on the shore of Lake Keowee, the park keeps the 1.4-mile Natural Bridge trail and the longer Raven Rock trail.

moments.title: Table Rock State Park
moments.text: Two companies of World War I veterans began the park for the CCC, were apparently too old for the mountain work, and gave way in 1936 to junior companies, who built the log lodge.
